question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total freight carried by Canadian railways in July 2026, in tonnes, as it will be first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (total traffic carried, Canada).

target.what: Total freight tonnage carried by Canadian railways in July 2026, Canada, as first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (total traffic carried).
target.caveats: Working interpretation: revenue freight tonnage carried by Canadian railways reporting to Statistics Canada, all commodities and intermodal traffic where included in the published total, Canada-level, for the calendar month. This is not annual or year-to-date tonnage, not carloads or intermodal unit

candidates.hypothesis: The July 2026 total is best anchored by the same month in prior years and by recent 2026 monthly levels. July has recurring seasonal patterns related to grain, construction, and bulk shipments, so T_Jul2026 can be modelled from T_Jul2025, the year-over-year trend, and T_Jun2026.
candidates.data_to_find: Statistics Canada monthly total tonnes carried, Canada, for July 2019-2025 and January-June 2026 or the most recent months published before the cutoff; release dates and any revisions. Minimum evidence: July 2024 and July 2025 totals plus June 2026 total.

Canadian railways carried million tonnes June 2026

assessment.note: StatCan monthly/annual total-tonnage series show a consistent scale: July 2024 29.9 Mt just under the five-year July average 30.3 Mt; Dec 2025 31.0 Mt; Feb 2026 29.4 Mt; Mar 2025 33.3 Mt; Jun 2025 29.8 Mt; 2025 annual 376.6 Mt versus 377.3 Mt in 2024. Different months and seasonal positions are not contradictions; all share the same publisher and are not independent.

The component identity holds closely: Jul 2024 non-intermodal 23.2 + intermodal 2.8 + US connections 3.8 = 29.8 Mt versus total 29.9 Mt; Dec 2025 24.8 + 2.8 + 3.3 = 30.9 versus 31.0; Feb 2026 23.2 + 3.0 + 3.2 = 29.4 exactly. This supports modelling the national total as non-intermodal + intermodal + US-connection traffic plus a small residual.

US-connection tonnage was about 12% of total rail tonnage in 2023-24, fell to 10.4% in 2025, and recovered toward 11% in Jan-Feb 2026. Annual 2025 US tonnage fell 13.3% and March 2025 fell 16.1%, while Feb 2026 rose 16.1% from a low base. These are consistent with a still-below-2024 but recovering US-connection component.

CTRF/AAR weekly and cumulative 2025 Canadian rail traffic is consistent with StatCan-scale outcomes: Jun 2025 29.8 Mt, H1 2025 188.0 Mt, intermodal 3.2 Mt, US connections 3.1 Mt, and weekly carloads 86,414 plus intermodal units 73,206 in late July 2025. Scope differs (units/carloads versus tonnes), so this is contextual rather than a direct replacement.

CN weekly 2026 operations in late July show carloads 100,390 (-4.1%) and revenue ton-miles 4,287 (-2.3%), with car velocity -7%, train speed -4%, and dwell +11%. This is a negative directional signal for very late July 2026, but it covers only CN and may be year-over-year or week-over-week; it is not directly convertible to national monthly tonnes without carrier-share and load-factor bridges.

These are mostly repeated CEIC snapshots of 2019-2020 commodity, intermodal, and total-traffic series, often the same value repeated under different URLs. They establish historical scale and bounds but are COVID-era or otherwise stale and not independent of one another; they should not be combined as separate years in a current monthly median.

Commodity-level 2025 annual data and Feb 2026 potash/canola strength show which bulk groups were moving, but they are not July 2026 total-tonnage observations. They support directional judgement on grains, potash, coal, crude, and lumber rather than direct substitution.

Coal-industry evidence says Canadian railroads move over 30 Mt of coal annually, mostly for export through BC, but the data are old and do not provide a July 2026 rail-tonnage share. Useful only as a broad check that coal is a major component.

The 2019 CN strike and herbicide-window items are irrelevant to July 2026 tonnage. The 2026 Thunder Bay wildfire item is a possible shock indicator, but the area burned and distance from Thunder Bay do not quantify rail tonnage lost or days of corridor closure, so it cannot enter a numerical method without an exposure assumption.
Investment, a rail price index, and US grain/coal carloads are not Canadian total tonnage measures. They may inform background conditions but are not direct inputs to the target.

Main failure is a structural shift in 2025-2026 volumes.

p111.role: June 2025 total cargo carried by Canadian railways, metric tonnes per month

a7.role: factor for July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to June 2025 total

methods.rationale: Uses the latest available mid-2025 monthly total before the missing July 2025 gap, then applies a combined seasonal-plus-trend factor to reach July 2026. It provides a recent-level anchor distinct from July 2024 and the five-year average. Main failure modes are instability in June-to-July seasonality and uncertainty in the 13-month trend.

assumptions.name: July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 was 29.9 Mt (p16) and the five-year July average was 30.3 Mt (p18), implying near-flat trend. Annual 2025 was 376.6 Mt versus 377.3 Mt in 2024 (p62/p63, -0.2%), while early 2026 rebounded strongly (Feb 2026 29.4 Mt, +9.8% yoy, p190-p197). Offset by CN late-July 2026 carloads -4.1% and RTM -2.3% (p162-p164). A two-year factor near 1.03 is a modest net increase with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: p16 is a representative July base and there is no major strike, wildfire corridor closure, or port shutdown in July 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: StatCan July 2025 or July 2026 data showing July 2026 more than about 5% above or below July 2024, or documented multi-week rail disruption in July 2026.

assumptions.name: July 2026 non-intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 non-intermodal loadings were 23.2 Mt (p23). Full-year 2025 non-intermodal was 299.8 Mt, up 0.9% from 2024 (p67), while Feb 2026 non-intermodal was 23.2 Mt, up 8.3% yoy (p193-p194). Early-2026 strength and late-July CN softness roughly offset, supporting a modest two-year increase.
assumptions.applies_when: The commodity mix and July seasonality remain close to the 2024-2026 pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that July 2026 grain, coal, potash, or crude loadings fell sharply relative to 2024, or that Feb 2026 strength was not sustained.

assumptions.name: July 2026 intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 intermodal was 2.8 Mt, up 19.2% yoy (p19-p20). June 2025 intermodal was 3.2 Mt, up 8.7% (p113), and Feb 2026 intermodal was 3.0 Mt, up 15.0% yoy (p195-p196). The trend is clearly upward, so July 2026 is placed above July 2024, but not at the strongest early-2026 growth rate.
assumptions.applies_when: Container traffic continues the 2025-early-2026 upward trend and no port/terminal disruption shifts volumes.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp intermodal decline in July 2026 or a major container-port or rail-terminal closure.

assumptions.name: July 2026 US-connection tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 US-connection traffic was 3.8 Mt (p21). Full-year 2025 US connections fell 13.3% to 39.3 Mt and the share fell to 10.4% (p69, p201). Feb 2026 recovered 16.1% yoy to 3.2 Mt (p197-p198) but from a low base and still near the historical February average of 3.4 Mt (p199). A level below July 2024 is therefore central.
assumptions.applies_when: US rail connections continue recovering slowly but remain below their 2023-2024 share of total tonnage.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that US-connection tonnage in July 2026 returned to or exceeded the July 2024 level.

assumptions.name: Residual other/rounding tonnage in July 2026
assumptions.rationale: The published total is slightly above the sum of non-intermodal, intermodal, and US-connection tonnage: July 2024 shows a 0.1 Mt residual (p16 versus p23+p19+p21), Dec 2025 also about 0.1 Mt (p61 versus p64+p65+p66), and Feb 2026 is essentially exact (p190 versus p193+p195+p197). A small positive residual allowance is therefore appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: StatCan continues to include a small residual/rounding or other component not captured by the three published segments.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published July 2026 total exactly equal to the sum of the three components, or a negative/large residual.

assumptions.name: July 2026 total relative to the 2024 five-year July average
assumptions.rationale: The five-year July average as of 2024 was 30.3 Mt (p18), and July 2024 itself was just under that average. Annual 2025 was essentially flat versus 2024 (p62/p63), early 2026 was strong (p190), and late-July CN was soft (p162-p164). A near-average July 2026 with a wide range is the best central transfer.
assumptions.applies_when: The historical July average remains a useful seasonal baseline and 2026 is not an extreme deviation year.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a structural break in July 2026 volumes or a very different July seasonal pattern in 2025-2026.

assumptions.name: July 2026 total relative to June 2025
assumptions.rationale: June 2025 total was 29.8 Mt (p111). July is seasonally lower than June in the 2024 analogue (July 2024 29.9 Mt versus implied June 2024 about 30.75 Mt), but the 13-month trend includes the strong early-2026 rebound. A small net increase over June 2025 is central, with a wide range to cover both the seasonal decline and trend uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: The June-to-July seasonal pattern and the 2025-2026 trend are broadly stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that July 2026 is much weaker or stronger than June 2025 after adjusting for normal July seasonality.

Same source, so not independent confirmation.

assumptions.name: July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 was just below the five-year July average (p16 vs p18). 2025 annual tonnage was essentially flat vs 2024 (p62 vs p63, -0.2%). February 2026 was up 9.8% y/y (p191) but that is a winter month with strong potash/canola; July is dominated by grain, coal, potash and intermodal. CN late-July 2026 RTMs were -2.3% and carloads -4.1% (p163, p164), suggesting softness. Net: roughly flat to slightly up vs July 2024, with wide uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 has no major labour stoppage or sustained corridor closure beyond the wildfire disruption already visible in CN weekly data.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published July 2026 StatCan total outside roughly 27-33 Mt, or evidence of a national strike/port closure lasting weeks.

assumptions.name: July 2026 non-intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: Non-intermodal 2025 annual was +0.9% vs 2024 (p67). February 2026 commodity traffic was +8.3% y/y (p194) but driven by potash/canola seasonality. July bulk (grain, coal, potash, iron ore, crude) is mixed; CN carload weakness suggests flat to slightly up.
assumptions.applies_when: Bulk commodity flows in July 2026 are near their 2024-2025 trend without a major harvest-timing shift.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July 2026 non-intermodal component reported far from 22-26 Mt.

assumptions.name: July 2026 intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: Intermodal has been the growth segment: July 2024 +19.2% y/y (p20), 2025 annual 37.5 Mt (p68), February 2026 +15.0% y/y (p196), June 2025 +8.7% (p113). Continued growth is plausible but port/container cycle risk keeps the range wide.
assumptions.applies_when: Container volumes through Vancouver/Prince Rupert/Montreal remain near 2025-2026 trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: A reported July 2026 intermodal tonnage below ~2.8 Mt or above ~3.6 Mt.

assumptions.name: July 2026 US-connection tonnage relative to July 2024
assumptions.rationale: US-connection tonnage fell 13.3% in 2025 to 39.3 Mt (p69), the lowest since 2020, and its share fell from 12.0% (p75) to 10.4% (p201). February 2026 rebounded +16.1% y/y (p198) to 3.2 Mt, but remained below the five-year average (p199). A partial recovery from the 2025 trough leaves July 2026 below July 2024.
assumptions.applies_when: US-connection traffic continues its partial 2026 recovery without returning to 2023-2024 levels.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July 2026 US-connection tonnage above ~4.0 Mt or below ~2.8 Mt.

assumptions.name: Residual other/rounding tonnage in July 2026
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 components (p23+p19+p21 = 29.8 Mt) fall slightly short of the reported total (p16 = 29.9 Mt), implying a small residual of order 0.1 Mt from rounding and minor unpublished categories.
assumptions.applies_when: The published total continues to be the sum of the three published components plus a small residual.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that the published total includes a large fourth component not captured by p23, p19, p21.

assumptions.name: July 2026 total relative to the 2024 five-year July average
assumptions.rationale: July 2024 was just under the five-year July average (p16 vs p18). 2025 was flat vs 2024 (p62 vs p63). With CN late-July 2026 softness (p163, p164), July 2026 is plausibly near the historical July norm.
assumptions.applies_when: No structural break in July seasonality between 2024 and 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July 2026 total far from 27-33 Mt.

assumptions.name: July 2026 total relative to June 2025
assumptions.rationale: June 2025 was 29.8 Mt (p111), down 3.1% y/y. July is typically similar to or slightly above June in recent years (July 2024 29.9 Mt vs May 2024 32.0 Mt shows month-to-month variation). A ratio near 1 with wide range reflects the 13-month gap and seasonal differences.
assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 is near the mid-2025 monthly level, adjusted for seasonality.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July 2026 total far from 27-33 Mt.

methods.label: m1

p16.role: July 2024 total freight tonnage carried by Canadian railways, Canada, metric tonnes per month

a1.role: factor for July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to July 2024 total

methods.rationale: Anchors on the observed July 2024 StatCan total and applies a two-year change factor informed by flat 2025 annual tonnage, the February 2026 rebound, and CN's negative late-July 2026 weekly metrics. Main failure mode: the two-year gap is bridged by an assumption rather than an observed July 2025 base.

methods.label: m2

p23.role: July 2024 non-intermodal freight loadings, Canada, metric tonnes per month

p19.role: July 2024 intermodal shipments originating in Canada, metric tonnes per month

p21.role: July 2024 freight traffic arriving from the United States by rail, Canada, metric tonnes per month

a2.role: factor for July 2026 non-intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024

a3.role: factor for July 2026 intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024

a4.role: factor for July 2026 US-connection tonnage relative to July 2024

a5.role: small residual or other/rounding tonnage in the published July 2026 total

methods.rationale: Component build-up from the three published July 2024 channels, each scaled by a segment-specific two-year factor, plus a small residual. Segment factors reflect divergent trends: intermodal growing, US-connection traffic recovering from a 2025 trough, non-intermodal roughly flat. Failure mode: segment factors are assumptions, and the residual is small but uncertain.

methods.label: m3

p18.role: five-year average July total freight tonnage carried by Canadian railways as of 2024, metric tonnes per month

a6.role: factor for July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to the 2024 five-year July average

methods.rationale: Uses the five-year July average as a seasonal norm and applies a factor near 1, reflecting flat 2025 annual tonnage and CN's soft late-July 2026 metrics. Failure mode: the five-year average is a 2019-2023 window and may not reflect 2026 structure.

methods.label: m4

p111.role: June 2025 total cargo carried by Canadian railways, metric tonnes per month

a7.role: factor for July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to June 2025 total

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent observed mid-year monthly total (June 2025) and applies a factor near 1 to bridge to July 2026, accounting for seasonality and the 13-month gap. Failure mode: June-to-July seasonality and the long gap are not directly observed.

kept.name: July 2026 total freight tonnage relative to July 2024
kept.rationale: July 2024 was just below the five-year July average (p16 vs p18). 2025 annual tonnage was essentially flat vs 2024 (p62 vs p63, -0.2%). February 2026 was up 9.8% y/y (p191) but that is a winter month with strong potash/canola; July is dominated by grain, coal, potash and intermodal. CN late-July 202
kept.applies_when: July 2026 has no major labour stoppage or sustained corridor closure beyond the wildfire disruption already visible in CN weekly data.
kept.falsified_by: A published July 2026 StatCan total outside roughly 27-33 Mt, or evidence of a national strike/port closure lasting weeks.

kept.name: July 2026 non-intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024
kept.rationale: Non-intermodal 2025 annual was +0.9% vs 2024 (p67). February 2026 commodity traffic was +8.3% y/y (p194) but driven by potash/canola seasonality. July bulk (grain, coal, potash, iron ore, crude) is mixed; CN carload weakness suggests flat to slightly up.
kept.applies_when: Bulk commodity flows in July 2026 are near their 2024-2025 trend without a major harvest-timing shift.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 non-intermodal component reported far from 22-26 Mt.

kept.name: July 2026 intermodal tonnage relative to July 2024
kept.rationale: Intermodal has been the growth segment: July 2024 +19.2% y/y (p20), 2025 annual 37.5 Mt (p68), February 2026 +15.0% y/y (p196), June 2025 +8.7% (p113). Continued growth is plausible but port/container cycle risk keeps the range wide.
kept.applies_when: Container volumes through Vancouver/Prince Rupert/Montreal remain near 2025-2026 trend.
kept.falsified_by: A reported July 2026 intermodal tonnage below ~2.8 Mt or above ~3.6 Mt.

kept.name: July 2026 US-connection tonnage relative to July 2024
kept.rationale: US-connection tonnage fell 13.3% in 2025 to 39.3 Mt (p69), the lowest since 2020, and its share fell from 12.0% (p75) to 10.4% (p201). February 2026 rebounded +16.1% y/y (p198) to 3.2 Mt, but remained below the five-year average (p199). A partial recovery from the 2025 trough leaves July 2026 below
kept.applies_when: US-connection traffic continues its partial 2026 recovery without returning to 2023-2024 levels.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 US-connection tonnage above ~4.0 Mt or below ~2.8 Mt.

kept.name: Residual other/rounding tonnage in July 2026
kept.rationale: July 2024 components (p23+p19+p21 = 29.8 Mt) fall slightly short of the reported total (p16 = 29.9 Mt), implying a small residual of order 0.1 Mt from rounding and minor unpublished categories.
kept.applies_when: The published total continues to be the sum of the three published components plus a small residual.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that the published total includes a large fourth component not captured by p23, p19, p21.

kept.name: July 2026 total relative to the 2024 five-year July average
kept.rationale: July 2024 was just under the five-year July average (p16 vs p18). 2025 was flat vs 2024 (p62 vs p63). With CN late-July 2026 softness (p163, p164), July 2026 is plausibly near the historical July norm.
kept.applies_when: No structural break in July seasonality between 2024 and 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 total far from 27-33 Mt.

kept.name: July 2026 total relative to June 2025
kept.rationale: June 2025 was 29.8 Mt (p111), down 3.1% y/y. July is typically similar to or slightly above June in recent years (July 2024 29.9 Mt vs May 2024 32.0 Mt shows month-to-month variation). A ratio near 1 with wide range reflects the 13-month gap and seasonal differences.
kept.applies_when: July 2026 is near the mid-2025 monthly level, adjusted for seasonality.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 total far from 27-33 Mt.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
